newsitem.title: GERMANY: Country merchants buy N.Europe new crop rapeseed.
newsitem.headline: Country merchants buy N.Europe new crop rapeseed.

text.p: Country merchants and co-operatives in northern Europe are active in the new crop rapeseed market where prices have come down from peaks earlier this week, brokers said on Friday.
Crushers were reported to be adequately covered for the spring months in the run up to the harvest.
New crop rapeseed buyers free Hamburg were at 460 marks a tonne for July/August, down from 466 marks earlier this week, with sellers five marks higher.
Danish new crop buyers in Germany were at 477 marks and farmgate prices around 430.
May delivery old crop was in a 490-499 marks buyer/seller range free Hamburg after 500 marks traded.

Soybean prices fell after a U.S. Department of Agriculture report which saw higher Latin American, Indian and Chinese crops, and a lower dollar dragged global oilseeds prices down, but Chicago opened higher on new factors.
May on Matif was up five marks from last night at 490 and August was up three at 462 marks in thin volume.
In the products, rape oil was becoming competitive versus soy oil and rape meal was sought after by the feed industry, which boosted prices.
April buyers at points other than Hamburg were at 480-485 versus 485-495 last week, while August buyers were at 445-460 compared with 450-470.
March rape meal ex Hamburg mills was at 33.00-33.25 marks per 100 kg (32.50-32.75 last week), April was up 0.75 at 32.50 and May-first half July oil was up 0.50 marks at 31.50.
German rape oil sellers quoted April at 92.75 marks per 100 kg, off 0.25, and May-July at 93.75 marks, off 0.50.
